Grid and list views, artist photos, colors from the album art, and settings you can set from Nix. Under that, a long round of fixes to playback, downloads and settings from a full code review.

### Downloads

| File | For |
| --- | --- |
| `Ond-0.3.0-macos-universal.dmg` (or `.zip`) | macOS 11 or later, Apple silicon and Intel |
| `Ond-0.3.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | Linux on x86_64, glibc 2.39 or newer (Ubuntu 24.04, Fedora 40, Debian 13) |
| `Ond-0.3.0-linux-aarch64.tar.gz` | Linux on ARM64, same requirements |
| `Ond-0.3.0-windows-x86_64.zip` | Windows 10 and 11. Still untested on real hardware; issues welcome. |

On NixOS or with Nix: `nix profile install github:Solidsilver/ond/v0.3.0`. Install steps for every platform are in the [README](https://github.com/Solidsilver/ond#install).

### New

- Albums and Artists can be a grid or a list. The list is a table you sort by clicking its headers; click again to reverse. Artists sort by name, most albums or earliest year.
- Artists show their photo from the server, in the list and on their page. Artists the server has no photo of show their initial.
- An alphabet rail beside long lists sorted by name, to jump along them (Settings › Appearance › Lists, off by default).
- A new Appearance section in Settings: theme, an accent color (eight presets or your own), colors that follow the album art, blurred artwork behind the Player and Mini, and a waveform seek bar with adjustable bars.
- Settings › Library has a Cache group showing how much cover art and streamed audio is on disk, each with a Clear button.
- With Home Manager, the flake's new module (`programs.ond`) can set any of Ond's settings. Settings set there are locked in the app, and the rest stay editable. See [docs/home-manager.md](https://github.com/Solidsilver/ond/blob/main/docs/home-manager.md).
- Experimental (Settings › Experimental, all off by default): a live spectrum, a spectrogram in the Info tab, and a full-window visualizer (⌘T) with three styles.
- Emoji in titles show in color.
- A failed sign-in shows what the server, or the proxy in front of it, said.

### Playback

- Albums that mix 16- and 24-bit tracks at the same sample rate play gaplessly.
- The last notes of a track before a format change, and at the end of the queue, are no longer cut off.
- Playback no longer gets stuck buffering at the end of the queue.
- A seek can no longer leave playback silent.
- Playback follows a new system default device mid-track (headphones plugged in).
- A track no longer scrobbles twice when the output device changes.
- Synced lyrics with an offset shift the right way.

### Downloads and settings

- A downloads list that can't be read no longer deletes your downloads. Ond keeps the files and says so in Settings › Offline, with a way to clean up.
- Moving downloads to another folder runs in the background with progress, and a move interrupted by quitting finishes at the next start.
- Signing in to another account stops the old account's syncs and downloads, and no longer stalls the window.
- Settings and plays waiting to be scrobbled are written safely, so a power cut can't leave an empty settings file.
- Quitting never waits more than a couple of seconds on a stuck disk or keychain.

### Faster

- A 20,000-song playlist scrolls as smoothly as a short one.
- Covers on screen load before ones scrolled past.
- Lighter frames while playing, especially with a long queue.

### Smaller fixes

- macOS: dragging the volume slider no longer moves the window, and double-clicking the toolbar zooms without stretching the window.
- Linux: the waveform seek bar in the toolbar no longer runs into the artist line.
- Names starting with Ø, Ł, Æ and similar letters sort with their base letter.
- One malformed song, album or artist from the server is skipped instead of failing its whole page.
